segments.title: Chương 3: 0003 【Lắc Đầu Bay Tóc】
segments.content:
County Magistrate Xie was named Xie Yang, from a remote rural village in Fushi County, Longdu City.

His family was quite poor.

But he had an older brother named Xie Fei, who had passed the civil service exam several years ago, so their financial pressure had eased somewhat.

Xie Yang, wearing an ill-fitting old suit, hands in his pockets like an adult, kicked his own suitcase and asked, "You used your dad's suitcase for books, what about the clothes inside?"

Chen Guiliang said with disgust, "They all fucking reeked. The stench made me want to puke, so I just threw them in the foot basin."

"I was planning to take them home and throw them in the washing machine after the midterms," Xie Yang explained casually.

He had a center-parted hairstyle, with one side deliberately left especially long.

Usually, he tucked the hair behind his ear to get around the school rule against long hair. When the teachers weren't around, he could let it hang down, perfectly covering half of his eye.

The fellow, thinking himself very handsome, blew a puff of air, precisely clearing the hair from his eye. Then he feigned a suave move, flicking his hair to the side. "You son of a bitch, you handed in your paper so fast. How many math problems did you do?"

"Did jackshit," Chen Guiliang pointed to the remaining few books. "You buying books or not?"

Xie Yang flicked his hair again. "Not buying. Your books are my books, free for me to read anytime."

Chen Guiliang really wanted to hold his head down; all that damned flicking was annoying to watch.

Like he had a cervical spine problem.

Xie Yang's legs were also shaking nonstop. Seeing a girl walk by, he once again blew a puff of air and flicked his hair, trying to look cool.

Unfortunately, the girl didn't even give him a second glance.

From his suit to his leather shoes, Xie Yang's entire outfit was his brother's hand-me-downs. He raised his hand, revealing a cheap, broken watch, and glanced at the time. "The cafeteria is about to open."

"It's still early. Help me sell my books," Chen Guiliang remained seated cross-legged.

Xie Yang didn't refuse and quietly squatted down beside Chen Guiliang.

Chen Guiliang turned his head and squinted at him, finding it oddly amusing.

Right now, this guy's face was covered in acne, his body brimming with a pent-up, hormonal flamboyance he couldn't vent. Every move he made seemed so childish and idiotic.

Who would have thought he'd become a county magistrate in the future?

The future County Magistrate Xie, at this moment, picked up a book and flipped through it, blowing his hair as he bragged, "I reached level 33 in Mir 2. Yesterday, I got a top-tier helmet with +3 magic. You have no idea what a sensation it caused. Half the internet cafe crowded around to see it. The cafe manager offered 300 yuan, but I'm not stupid. What the hell can you buy for 300 yuan?"

Chen Guiliang sighed, "The World of Legend, ah. Such an ancient game."

Xie Yang said, "Ancient my ass. It's only been in open beta for a little over three months. Did you not wake up properly today?"

"You wouldn't understand."

Chen Guiliang's fingers trembled inexplicably. He couldn't help but ask, "Got a smoke?"

"When did you start smoking?" Xie Yang pulled out a pack of soft yellow Hongmei cigarettes and handed the whole pack to Chen Guiliang.

Chen Guiliang took it and looked. "Damn, only half a cigarette left. I thought you were being so generous."

Xie Yang argued, "What do you mean half a cigarette? It's clearly two-thirds of one."

Inside the crumpled cigarette pack, there was indeed two-thirds of a cigarette, along with a plastic lighter.

Chen Guiliang didn't mind that it had been smoked. He stuck it in his mouth and lit it.

He wasn't a heavy smoker, but right now he just wanted one to calm his nerves with nicotine.

"Are you trying to get killed, smoking here!" Xie Yang was terrified, furtively looking around. He only relaxed when he saw there were no teachers nearby.

Perhaps because he now had someone to confide in, and the cigarette was soothing his mood, Chen Guiliang had a bellyful of words he wanted to let out.

"Do you believe in supernatural events?" Chen Guiliang asked.

Xie Yang shot back, "Did you see a ghost?"

Chen Guiliang said, "It could also be a sci-fi event."

"A UFO, then," Xie Yang reached over to grab the cigarette. "Leave me a couple of drags."

Chen Guiliang passed him the cigarette. "Ah, forget it. This thing is impossible to explain."

Xie Yang took a deep drag from the cigarette butt, then handed what was left back. "Got tangled up with a female ghost? After you're done, let me have a go."

Even the female ghosts would be rendered speechless by you guys. Chen Guiliang didn't take the cigarette back. "If you're that damn pent-up, you can go to the wet market and buy a slab of pork belly to sort yourself out. The feel of it is no different from getting a hooker."

"For real?" Xie Yang actually wanted to confirm this information.

Chen Guiliang patted him on the shoulder. "When I'm financially free, I'll buy you pork belly every day."

"Get the hell out of here," Xie Yang finished the last few drags of the cigarette and said mysteriously, "Zhou Jing smiled at me at noon today. Do you think she's into me?"

Who was Zhou Jing?

Chen Guiliang thought hard and soon had a faint impression. "What could she possibly be into you for? Because you flick your hair so suavely? Or does she find your acne-covered face particularly handsome?"

"You son of a bitch, if you don't know how to talk, then shut up!" Xie Yang became angry from embarrassment.

Chen Guiliang chuckled.

Returning to high school was quite interesting. It was a pity it was senior year; it would have been even better to go back to freshman year.

Although he was poor, he could still live a carefree life.

"Thump, thump, thump..."

A boy came over dribbling a basketball. He was over 1.9 meters tall and rather handsome. Guys like him were extremely popular with girls at school.

He had an MP3 player hanging around his neck, listening to music with earbuds in.

In 2003, this kind of electronic device was as cool as a brand-name mobile phone.

But Chen Guiliang and Xie Yang both frowned in unison.

In every class, there was always one or two assholes.

The asshole dribbling the basketball towards them was named Li Jun. His grandfather was a factory director at a textile mill before retiring, his parents were minor leaders within the system, and he had a whole bunch of relatives in the system too.

A county-town Brahmin!

How much of a bastard was this guy?

After graduating from a junior college, his family arranged for him to be a bank teller. He would actually brag in the class group chat every so often: how many customers I yelled at yesterday, which leader I talked back to today.

He even deliberately made things difficult for elderly people doing their banking and described it in detail in the class group chat as a joke.

"Yo, selling scraps?"

As Li Jun passed the bookstall, he, not surprisingly, ran his mouth, standing there and taunting, "There's a shed over on East Street, specially for resettling laid-off workers. You two can go set up a shoeshine stand there."

Xie Yang was only 1.7 meters tall. Standing in front of the 1.9-meter-tall Li Jun, his presence was naturally suppressed.

Xie Yang subconsciously took half a step back, but he wouldn't be outdone verbally, muttering "moron" under his breath.

Of course, Chen Guiliang wouldn't stand for it either. He had to maintain his high school persona; his personality couldn't change too quickly.

So, Chen Guiliang's mouth was even fouler. "East Street isn't suitable. I can recommend your mom to Shijiakou (a cheap red-light district)."

"Fuck your mother!"

"Say that again if you dare!"

Li Jun was triggered by this, throwing down his basketball in anger and rolling up his sleeves to get rough.

Chen Guiliang patted his butt and stood up, taunting, "Wanna fight? I've got a pile of demerits. A barefoot man isn't afraid of one with shoes. I'll take you down even if I get expelled!"

Xie Yang also clenched his fists and glared at Li Jun. "Our Great Hero Chen chopped someone up in junior high. Someone like you? Old Chen could take on ten of you with a watermelon knife!"

Li Jun was a bully who picked on the weak and feared the strong. Seeing this, he immediately chickened out, turning to pick up his basketball while muttering to himself, "I won't lower myself to the level of country folk."

To be honest, Chen Guiliang couldn't understand the thought process of people like him.

Li Jun clearly didn't dare to fight Chen Guiliang, yet because of some minor conflict in their second year of high school, he kept coming over to provoke him again and again.

It seemed as if he wouldn't feel right if he didn't run his mouth a few times upon seeing him.

Meanwhile, after walking some distance away, the asshole Li Jun took out his phone to make a call. "Hello, Mom. I finished my math exam... I didn't do so well, mainly because someone distracted me... Yeah, right, it's that Chen Guiliang again. He's on probation and still can't behave. He turned in his paper less than half an hour in. It made me think a lot of time had passed, so I got flustered and started writing nonsense... Mom, guess what he went to do after turning in his paper early? He was actually collecting scraps and set up a stall in the school. A peasant is a peasant, hahaha..."

Chen Guiliang, unaware that someone was badmouthing him behind his back, glanced at the six books left in the suitcase and couldn't be bothered to sell them anymore. "Let's go out for stir-fry. My treat today."

"Your treat my ass. Save it for the cafeteria," Xie Yang knew Chen Guiliang was very poor.

Chen Guiliang pulled out the money from selling the books. "Your grandpa struck it rich today."

Xie Yang didn't refuse this time, only saying, "My treat next time."

The two of them dragged the battered old suitcase, bullshitting their way towards the school gate.

By now, more and more students were leaving after handing in their papers. Several of them greeted Chen Guiliang, all calling him by his nickname, "Great Hero Chen."

Chen Guiliang had a vague impression of these students, but couldn't remember most of their names.

"Great Hero Chen! Xie the Flirt!"

A skinny guy with a buzz cut, shouting Chen Guiliang's and Xie Yang's nicknames, came running towards them, bouncing enthusiastically.
